text: Given the connector is running, When a client sends tools/list, Then the response includes exactly the 18 digitalocean_apps_* tools named in the tech design's Data & API contract table, each with a first-line description <= 100 chars and full description <= 500 chars
Given tools/list, Then every tool's readOnlyHint/destructiveHint/idempotentHint matches the tech design's tool table

Given a tools/call request with no X-DigitalOcean-Api-Token header, When any tool is invoked, Then the response is HTTP 401 listing the required header, and the upstream DigitalOcean client is never called
Given a mocked upstream with more than 50 apps, When digitalocean_apps_list_apps is called with no arguments, Then it returns at most 50 apps and has_more is true
Given a mocked upstream with more than 200 apps, When digitalocean_apps_list_apps is called with limit=500, Then it returns at most 200 apps (the hard cap), not 500
Given a valid token and a real existing app id, When digitalocean_apps_get_app is called, Then it returns that app's current spec and active deployment id
steps: Obtain a real DigitalOcean API token with at least one existing app in the account
Start the connector locally with the real token in X-DigitalOcean-Api-Token
Call tools/call digitalocean_apps_get_app with that app's real id
expect: Response contains the app's spec and an active_deployment object with an id and phase field, matching what the DigitalOcean control panel shows for that app
notes: needs a real vendor account; recorded as pending in the Self-test report, not blocking per mcp-track.md section 3

text: Given a mocked upstream 404 for an unknown app id, When digitalocean_apps_get_app is called, Then it returns a structured not_found error, not an HTTP 500

Given a real token and an app spec with an invalid region, When digitalocean_apps_create_app is called, Then DigitalOcean's own validation error is surfaced as invalid_argument with DigitalOcean's message
steps: Start the connector locally with a real DigitalOcean API token
Call tools/call digitalocean_apps_create_app with a spec using a region slug that does not exist
expect: Response is {"error": {"code": "invalid_argument", ...}} and the message text matches DigitalOcean's own validation error, not a generic failure
notes: needs a real vendor account; recorded as pending in the Self-test report, not blocking

text: Given the registered tool description for digitalocean_apps_update_app, Then it states PUT-replace semantics (unspecified fields are not partially merged)

Given the digitalocean_apps_delete_app tool definition, Then its only required argument is a single app_id (no name or filter argument), destructiveHint is true, and its description contains the word irreversible

Given a mocked upstream, When digitalocean_apps_restart_app is called with no component_names, Then the restart request carries no component filter (restarts all); When called with component_names=["web"], Then the request carries that filter

Given a mocked upstream 409 conflict on create_deployment (deployment already in progress), When digitalocean_apps_create_deployment is called, Then the result is a structured upstream_error and the call is not retried as if transient

Given a mocked upstream, When digitalocean_apps_get_logs is called with app_id only, Then it calls the aggregate active-deployment logs endpoint; When called with both deployment_id and component_name, Then it calls the most specific per-component deployment logs endpoint
Given digitalocean_apps_get_logs is called with log_type="not-a-real-type", Then it returns invalid_argument without calling the upstream API

Given a real app with at least two deployments, When digitalocean_apps_manage_rollback is called with action=start then action=commit using the deployment_id returned by start, Then the app rolls back to the earlier deployment; When action=commit is called without a prior start's deployment_id, Then it is rejected as invalid_argument
steps: Start the connector locally with a real DigitalOcean API token against an app with 2+ deployments
Call digitalocean_apps_manage_rollback(action="start", app_id=...) and capture the returned deployment_id
Separately, call digitalocean_apps_manage_rollback(action="commit", app_id=..., deployment_id omitted or invalid)
expect: After commit, the app's active deployment is the earlier one; the commit-without-a-prior-start call returns {"error": {"code": "invalid_argument", ...}}
notes: needs a real vendor account; recorded as pending in the Self-test report, not blocking

text: Given digitalocean_apps_get_deployment_options() and digitalocean_apps_validate_spec(spec=...), Then both succeed with no app_id argument supplied and both are readOnlyHint true

Given two concurrent tools/call requests carrying different X-DigitalOcean-Api-Token values (token A and token B), When both complete, Then the outbound Authorization header captured for each matches only its own request's token, never the other's

Given a mocked upstream that returns 429 with Retry-After once then 200, When a tool is called, Then it succeeds after one backoff delay; Given a mocked upstream that returns 429 for the whole retry budget, Then the tool returns a structured rate_limited error rather than hanging
Given README.md's MSPbots Connector section, Then it is byte-for-byte identical to reference/readme-connector-section.md from the vendor-mcp-development skill
Given README.md, Then it documents X-DigitalOcean-Api-Token in a header table including a token-creation path
